import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov
subgroups?

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«10.78»

/--
A Chernikov group is a virtually abelian group satisfying the minimal
condition on subgroups. The latter condition says that there is no infinite
strictly descending chain of subgroups.
-/
def IsChernikovGroup (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∃ A : Subgroup G, IsMulCommutative A ∧ A.FiniteIndex) ∧
    WellFounded ((· < ·) : Subgroup G → Subgroup G → Prop)

/--
Does there exist a non-Chernikov group $G$ with Chernikov subgroups $A$ and
$B$ such that $G = AB$? Here $AB = \{ab \mid a \in A, b \in B\}$ is the
setwise product; neither subgroup is assumed to be normal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsChernikovGroup A ∧ IsChernikovGroup B ∧
        (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ ∧ ¬ IsChernikovGroup G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.78»
modeling_decisions: Defined a Chernikov group using the standard equivalent characterization from the decomposition notes: a virtually abelian group satisfying the minimal condition on subgroups.
Expressed virtual abelianness by the existence of an abelian finite-index subgroup; normality is not required, since the finite-index core gives the equivalent normal formulation.
Expressed the minimal condition as well-foundedness of strict inclusion on `Subgroup G`, ruling out infinite strictly descending subgroup chains.
Interpreted `G` being the product of `A` and `B` as the pointwise set equality `(A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ`, without assuming either factor normal.

new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no predicate for Chernikov groups, while the conjecture requires it for the ambient group and both factor subgroups.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.78

by V. P. Shunkov

Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

A Chernikov group is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer
(quasicyclic) $p$-groups. Equivalently, it is a group with an abelian subgroup of finite
index that satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups. Here "product" means the setwise
product $AB = G$ of two subgroups; neither factor is assumed to be normal. When both factors
are normal the product is Chernikov by a classical theorem of Chernikov.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Kourovka.«10.78»

/--
A group $G$ is a *Chernikov group* if it is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely
many Prüfer (quasicyclic) $p$-groups. By a theorem of Chernikov (see D. J. S. Robinson,
*A Course in the Theory of Groups*, Sections 4.2 and 5.4), this holds if and only if $G$ has an
abelian subgroup of finite index and satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups, that is,
there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups of $G$. We use this
characterisation as the definition. In particular every finite group is Chernikov.
-/
def IsChernikov (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  (∃ N : Subgroup G, N.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative N) ∧ WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)

/-- Every finite group is a Chernikov group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem isChernikov_of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsChernikov G :=
  ⟨⟨⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩, inferInstance⟩

/-- The infinite cyclic group is not a Chernikov group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_isChernikov_multiplicative_int : ¬ IsChernikov (Multiplicative ℤ) := by
  rintro ⟨-, h⟩
  refine not_strictAnti_of_wellFoundedLT
    (fun n => AddSubgroup.toSubgroup (AddSubgroup.zmultiples ((2 : ℤ) ^ n))) ?_
  refine strictAnti_nat_of_succ_lt fun n => ?_
  rw [OrderIso.lt_iff_lt, SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists]
  refine ⟨AddSubgroup.zmultiples_le_of_mem ?_, 2 ^ n, AddSubgroup.mem_zmultiples _, ?_⟩
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    exact dvd_mul_right _ _
  · rw [Int.mem_zmultiples_iff, pow_succ]
    intro h
    have := Int.le_of_dvd (by positivity) h
    nlinarith [pow_pos (show (0 : ℤ) < 2 by norm_num) n]

/--
Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

That is, is there a group $G$ with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that $A$ and $B$ are Chernikov
groups, $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$, and $G$ is not a Chernikov group? Neither $A$
nor $B$ is assumed to be normal in $G$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsChernikov A ∧ IsChernikov B ∧ (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ ∧
        ¬ IsChernikov G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.78»

This is equivalent to the textbook definition 'finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer p-groups' by Kurosh's classification of abelian groups with Min together with Chernikov's theorem (Robinson, A Course in the Theory of Groups, §4.2 and §5.4); the direct Prüfer-product formulation was avoided because Mathlib has no Prüfer-group type and it would require a much heavier ∃-over-types-and-MulEquiv encoding. A reviewer should confirm they accept this equivalent characterisation as the definition.
The minimal condition on subgroups is encoded as WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) (no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups / every nonempty family of subgroups has a minimal member).

'Product of two subgroups' is the setwise product (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ (open scoped Pointwise), with neither A nor B assumed normal, following the decomposition notes. Since A, B are subgroups this is symmetric (AB = G ⇔ BA = G).

The existential ranges over G : Type (universe 0), matching the other Kourovka files (1.74, 19.25); Chernikov groups and their products are countable, so this loses nothing.
Two proved @[category test] lemmas are included as API sanity checks for the bespoke definition: every finite group is Chernikov, and Multiplicative ℤ is not Chernikov.

A *Chernikov group* is a finite extension of a direct product of finitely many Prüfer
(quasicyclic) $p$-groups. Equivalently, it is a group satisfying the minimal condition on
subgroups that has an abelian subgroup of finite index. The equivalence follows from
Kurosh's theorem: an abelian group satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups if and only
if it is a direct product of finitely many quasicyclic groups and finite cyclic groups
(see D. J. S. Robinson, *A Course in the Theory of Groups*, Sections 4.2 and 5.4).

The product $AB$ of two subgroups $A$ and $B$ is the set $\{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$.
The subgroups are not assumed to be normal: a product of two normal Chernikov subgroups is
always a Chernikov group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.78»

open scoped Pointwise

/--
A group $G$ is a *Chernikov group* if it satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups
(every non-empty set of subgroups has a minimal element, i.e. `<` is well-founded on
`Subgroup G`) and has an abelian subgroup of finite index.

Equivalently, $G$ has a normal subgroup of finite index which is a direct product of
finitely many Prüfer $p$-groups.
-/
def IsChernikov (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) ∧ ∃ A : Subgroup G, A.FiniteIndex ∧ IsMulCommutative A

/-- Every finite group is a Chernikov group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsChernikov.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsChernikov G :=
  ⟨inferInstance, ⊥, inferInstance, inferInstance⟩

/--
Does there exist a non-Chernikov group which is a product of two Chernikov subgroups?

That is, is there a group $G$ with Chernikov subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that
$G = AB = \{ab : a \in A,\ b \in B\}$ while $G$ itself is not a Chernikov group?
The subgroups $A$ and $B$ are not assumed to be normal.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.78» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (A B : Subgroup G),
      IsChernikov A ∧ IsChernikov B ∧ (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ ∧
      ¬ IsChernikov G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.78»

The finite-index abelian subgroup is not required to be normal (its normal core is a normal finite-index abelian subgroup, so this is equivalent).
Minimal condition on subgroups is encoded as WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G); verified in a scratch file that this is equivalent to 'every nonempty set of subgroups has a minimal element'.

'Product of two subgroups' is the setwise product (A : Set G) * (B : Set G) = Set.univ (Mathlib idiom, cf.
